hood_desc: The pedestrianized main street lined with boutiques, restaurants, and the clifftop Piazza IX Aprile terrace; the natural base for any visit.
A dramatic hilltop village a short drive above Taormina, offering sweeping views back down at the coast.
The harbor and beach area below Taormina, connected by cable car, popular for swimming and boat trips.

The beach town in the bay directly below Taormina, with a long seafront promenade of hotels, lidos, pizzerias and bars, and the Naxos archaeological park on the headland at its southern end. Rooms cost noticeably less than up in Taormina and buses run up the hill in about 15 minutes.

landmarks: Teatro Antico (Ancient Greek Theatre)
A 3rd-century-BC theatre carved into the hillside, its ruined columns framing smoking Mount Etna and the Ionian Sea, Sicily's most sublime stage.
Isola Bella
A tiny pearl-shaped island nature reserve tethered to a pebble beach by a slender sandbar, Taormina's most beloved swimming and photo spot.
Corso Umberto
The elegant pedestrian spine threading between medieval gates, lined with palazzi, ceramic shops and granita cafés made famous by The White Lotus.
Piazza IX Aprile
Taormina's chequerboard-paved terrace-square, where baroque churches and the Wunderbar café open onto a balustrade view of Etna and the coast.
Villa Comunale (Parco Duca di Cesarò)
Lush public gardens created by an eccentric Englishwoman, where follies and subtropical blooms overlook the sparkling Ionian far below.
Duomo di Taormina (Cathedral of San Nicolò)
A fortress-like 13th-century cathedral fronted by a baroque fountain bearing the town's curious two-legged centaur emblem.
Palazzo Corvaja
A 10th-century Arab-Norman palace of crenellated stone and mullioned windows, once seat of Sicily's parliament, anchoring Corso Umberto's entrance.
Santuario Madonna della Rocca
A tiny rock-hewn church perched on a crag above town, reached by an old stone stairway with breathtaking views over Taormina's rooftops.
Castelmola
A dreamy medieval village crowning the mountain above Taormina, famed for almond wine, castle ruins and vertiginous panoramas of Etna and two seas.
Mazzarò Beach and Cable Car
Taormina's iconic funivia swoops from town to this pretty pebble cove, gateway to boat trips along grottoed cliffs toward Isola Bella.

train.note: No international trains. Taormina-Giardini station is down at sea level, about 200 m below the town, with frequent regional trains to Catania in around 45 minutes and Messina in 40; local buses and a cable car climb up to the centre. Long-distance Intercity trains to Rome and Naples cross the Strait of Messina by train ferry. Regional tickets are fixed-price with no need to book ahead.

bus.note: No international coaches. Interbus (https://www.interbus.it/) runs frequent buses from the Taormina bus terminal on Via Pirandello directly to Catania and its airport in about 1h20 - often more convenient than the train because they drop you in the town itself rather than at the seaside station. Other services reach Messina and Giardini Naxos.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from Taormina. Small boats from Giardini Naxos and Mazzarò run summer excursions to Isola Bella and along the coast, which are sightseeing trips rather than transport. The nearest scheduled sailings are the Aeolian Islands hydrofoils from Milazzo, about two hours north.

half.name: Alcantara Gorges
half.blurb: Narrow volcanic rock canyon carved by a cold mountain river, walkable in shallow sections.

full.name: Mount Etna
full.blurb: Active volcano with cable car and jeep excursions across its lava fields and craters.

full.name: Syracuse
full.blurb: Ancient Greek city with a well-preserved Greek theater and the old island quarter of Ortigia.

notes.walk: The historic center along Corso Umberto is pedestrian and very walkable; Isola Bella beach is reached by a cable car from town
notes.card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small shops and the beach cable car
notes.safety: Very safe town, popular with visitors of all ages. Petty theft in crowded areas during peak season is the main concern.
notes.religion: Roman Catholic (majority); no religious affiliation (growing minority)
notes.net: Strong 4G/5G coverage citywide. Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes. ~€10-20 for a 10-20GB prepaid tourist SIM. Free wifi widely available. A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM.
notes.transit: Interbus regional coaches and a cable car (funivia) linking the town to Mazzarò and Isola Bella beach
notes.transport: Catania-Fontanarossa Airport (CTA), about 1 hr away. Taormina-Giardini train station on the coastal line, a short bus/taxi ride up to town. Interbus coaches connect to Catania, Messina, and the airport. Reachable via the A18 motorway; parking in the historic center is very limited.
